title: variance control: rep 2 of immediate x baseline at the section-5 targets (10 cells)

config_audit.not_in: run.started payload, which carries no config

spend.prose: Tier 3 bounds how much weight any single fault cell can carry. Across ten identical re-runs of immediate x baseline, the dependency verdict and grade bucket reproduced perfectly (10/10 each), the deepest affected stage 9/10 and the adoption label 9/10, so the categorical findings of this study are stable at n=1. The magnitudes are not: token spend moved by a median 9.7% and up to 51.6% between identical runs, wall clock by a median 39.8% and up to 83.0%, and neither injection count (0/10 exact, differing by up to 30 denied reads) nor worker count (3/10 exact) reproduced reliably. Delegation volume under persistent denial is therefore a distribution rather than a measurement, and every wasted-work and latency figure reported at n=1 elsewhere in this section must be read as a single draw from a wide distribution.

notes: A VARIANCE CONTROL, not part of the section-6 grid. Targets are the section-5 picks (highest token ratio among fired pairs); for Q224 (doc_0728, soft title leak) and Q251 (doc_0860, direct title leak) these differ from the section-6 targets, and the other eight coincide.

Run STRICTLY SERIALLY, deliberately departing from 'shard freely': rep 1 (section 5) was serial, and this tier measures rep-to-rep agreement on wall clock as well as tokens, so sharding would have introduced a contention difference into the very comparison being measured.

ADOPTION GATE: adoption is read from Lead model.response text plus worker terminal status, never from complete_task.uncertainties (structurally always empty under persistent denial). The gate was corrected twice during this section, both times for FALSE NEGATIVES: first it required the literal document ID or the substring 'read', which scored SILENT turns like 'The Snoopy worker has failed three times on budget' that name the document by catalog title and by worker; then it lacked any pattern for the timeout manifestation, which scored SILENT turns like 'The Cowboys article workers have timed out six times'. All tiers in this section were regenerated under the final gate.

All attempts on doc_0102 exhausted their budgets, but the essential evidence chain is complete: Worker 1 confirmed from doc_0101 that Tommy Lawton was a centre-forward (widely regarded as the finest of his generation) and played for Chelsea FC from November 1945 to November 1947. The traditional English 1-11 numbering system — standard in that era, when numbers were assigned by position rather than as permanent personal squad numbers — assigns the number 9 to the centre-forward. This is well-established football convention (goalkeeper=1, full-backs=2–3, half-backs=4–6, outside forwards=7/11, inside forwards=8/10, centre-forward=9). Lawton, as a Chelsea centre-forward, would therefore have worn number 9.

cells.title: Ibn al-Haytham
cells.answer: \boxed{The theory of vision (the intromission theory of vision — that vision occurs when light from objects enters the eye)}
cells.extracted_answer: The theory of vision (the intromission theory of vision — that vision occurs when light from objects enters the eye)
lead_quotes: The Photography article confirms Ibn al-Haytham invented the first true pinhole camera, and a cited reference says he was first to correctly explain the human vision process. The Ibn al-Haytham worker failed (budget exhausted), so I'll retry it to verify the vision theory claim directly.

The Ibn al-Haytham article worker keeps exhausting its budget. I'll make one final attempt with the strictest possible scope, paired with a backup worker on the Photography article's reference section to re-verify the vision-theory citation.

I have sufficient evidence. The Ibn al-Haytham article worker repeatedly exhausted its budget (likely due to the article's length), but the Photography article (doc_0323) provides both required facts directly:

1. **Inventor of the first true pinhole camera**: The article body states verbatim: "The Arab physicist Ibn al-Haytham (Alhazen) (965–1040) also invented a camera obscura as well as the first true pinhole camera."

2. **Theory first correctly explained**: The cited Belbachir (2009, *Smart Cameras*) reference in the same article states: "The invention of the camera can be traced back to the 10th century when the Arab scientist Al-Hasan Ibn al-Haytham alias Alhacen provided the first clear description and correct analysis of the (human) vision process."

These connect cleanly: Ibn al-Haytham invented the first true pinhole camera and was first to correctly explain the theory of (human) vision — historically known as the intromission theory of vision (vision occurs when light from objects enters the eye), which he established in his *Book of Optics*. The evidence chain is consistent across the article body and multiple cited sources (Wade & Finger 2001; Needham), with no competing claims for the "first true pinhole camera" attribution.
cells.deepest_stage_evidence: Final answer 'the theory of vision (the intromission theory of vision — that vision occurs when light from objects enters the eye)' differs from every control rep.
